item.title: Forensic protocol — from narrative to reproducible case
item.lead: A subsequent edition can be significantly strengthened by treating each case as a small digital investigation dossier.

blocks.text: Step A: preserve the source file unchanged and create a cryptographic hash. Step B: record the date, source, method of acquisition, and any permissions. Step C: create a timeline of account, chat, payment, and personnel events. Step D (IP discrepancies): compare identity, IP, device, login role, and sending times. Step E: link each fact to a source ID.

For CRM research, personal data must be minimized. Researchers do not necessarily need the content of all private conversations to prove that a team operates with spending tiers or scripts. A scheme with anonymized identifiers can demonstrate the same mechanism with less privacy risk.

For financial reconstruction, payment data must be separated from interpretation. A series of micropayments in itself is not proof of carding or money laundering. Additional signals are required for this, such as chargeback patterns, account linkages, anomalous device signals, processor alerts, bank investigations, or criminal justice documents.

blocks.label: CHAIN OF CUSTODY
blocks.text: Without provenance, integrity, and a timeline of a digital artifact, a screenshot remains illustrative rather than forensically decisive.
